Bijan Robinson|RB.role: Workhorse RB1, arguably the best back in football in 2025: league-leading 2,298 scrimmage yards and 11 TDs on 366 touches (17 games), 5.1 YPC, plus 79 rec / 820 rec yds on 103 targets. Tyler Allgeier left in free agency (now in Arizona); Atlanta added Brian Robinson Jr. (1-yr/$2.5M) as a physical change-of-pace, leaving Bijan with no real threat to his volume.
Bijan Robinson|RB.strength: Legitimate No. 1-overall pick case in redraft and dynasty — generational talent + bellcow volume + scheme fit. Bust path is mild: if the receiving role shrinks meaningfully and Atlanta's offense sputters with QB instability, he could be "merely" a back-end RB1 rather than the runaway RB1.
Bijan Robinson|RB.weakness: Receiving-volume regression under Stefanski's script; team-wide scoring/QB instability (Tua vs Penix-ACL) capping TDs; heavy 2025 workload. Age (24) and contract are non-issues.
Bijan Robinson|RB.key_capture: 7/26: Unsigned but attending normally — a payday-timing story, not a workload one. The resurfaced 'Bijan is third-string' headline is stale 2023 rookie-year noise; Brian Robinson Jr. is the handcuff and no threat to the lead role.
handcuff_candidates: KR/ST + passing-down depth) and Nathan Carter (camp competition). Allgeier no longer in the room.

Jahmyr Gibbs|RB.role: True bellcow for the first time in his career — Dan Campbell explicitly declared him the "bellcow" at OTAs (6/04), and RB coach Tashard Choice says this is the best Gibbs has looked in his career and is eager to hand him a bigger workload. 2025: 1,223 rush yds, 77 rec / 616 rec yds, 18 total TDs, 366.9 PPR points (finished RB3). Jahmyr Gibbs|RB.strength: Legit RB1-overall case for 2026 — bellcow workload + receiving role + elite environment. Likely beats his ADP if the offense stays healthy; main thing that caps him is Detroit's many mouths (St. Brown, LaPorta) keeping his red-zone TD share from running away.
Jahmyr Gibbs|RB.weakness: Pacheco vulturing goal-line TDs; minor frame/durability concern at heavy volume; some new-OC scheme-transition variance. Age (23) and contract are non-issues — Detroit picked up his fifth-year option (~$14.2M for 2027); he's extension-eligible next summer and is projected to become the highest-paid RB in NFL history, so no holdout risk.
Jahmyr Gibbs|RB.key_capture: 7/19: Bell-cow status official on the record; fifth-year option picked up and a record extension projected next summer removes holdout risk. 7/26 confirms unsigned-but-attending — payday timing, not workload.

Bryce Young|QB.role: Entering Year 4 as Carolina's starter (fifth-year option already picked up); new OC Brad Idzik takes over playcalling in 2026 after Canales called plays in 2025, but volume stays QB2-caliber — Young attempted 25 or fewer passes in half his 16 2025 starts and has never averaged 200 pass yds/game for a full season (FantasyPros, published 2026-07-09).
Bryce Young|QB.strength: Set career highs in 2025 (63.6% comp, 3,011 yds, 23 TD) and cut sack rate to a career-low 5.4%, showing incremental progression (FantasyPros).
Bryce Young|QB.weakness: Efficiency still bottom-of-class — career 6.0 YPA and 3.5% TD rate rank 22nd of 22 qualifying QBs over the last three seasons; finished QB29/QB23/QB24 in fantasy PPG across his three years as starter (CBS Sports, published 2026-06-08).

Daniel Jones|QB.role: Unquestioned QB1 entering 2026 camp per Colts.com (Jul 14, 2026); Anthony Richardson Sr. and Riley Leonard are competing behind him for the QB2 job, splitting reps evenly in OTAs. Colts re-signed/tagged Jones in March 2026 (transition tag, per CBS Sports) before finalizing a new contract. Over the first 10 weeks of 2025 (pre-injury) he ran as a legitimate high-volume starter — CBS Sports notes he was QB5 in fantasy scoring during that 8-2 start — giving him both pass-volume and rushing-floor upside when healthy under Shane Steichen.
Daniel Jones|QB.strength: Proven dual-threat production ceiling shown in the first half of 2025 (MVP-candidate-level play, rushing floor intact) when fully healthy.
Daniel Jones|QB.weakness: Coming off a torn right Achilles (injured Week 14, Dec 7, 2025, surgically repaired); a mid-2025 fibula fracture also sapped his mobility/passing effectiveness before the Achilles injury, so durability is the central question mark, not talent.

Omar Cooper Jr.|WR.strength: Physicality and sure hands on contested/difficult catches; strong yards-after-catch, averaging 7+ YAC and breaking a tackle on roughly a third of his receptions (Deebo Samuel Sr.-like profile).
Omar Cooper Jr.|WR.weakness: Crowded target competition in the slot/middle of the field (Isaiah Williams, TE Mason Taylor, TE Kenyon Sadiq, Arian Smith) muddies target share projection for anyone not named Wilson.

Hunter Henry|TE.role: Lead/starter TE in New England's passing game under OC Josh McDaniels; per SI (pub. 2026-05-06), caught 69-of-102 targets for 880 yards and 8 TDs in 2025 (9th among fantasy TEs, ~5 targets/game); CBS (pub. 2026-06-08) cites 768 yards, 7 TDs, 10.5 PPR points/game as his best output since arriving in NE in 2021 — the two sources disagree on exact 2025 counting stats (880 vs 768 yards, 8 vs 7 TDs), flagged as a source conflict below.

Hunter Henry|TE.weakness: 2025 fantasy value leaned on TD rate (7-8 TDs) that's hard to repeat, and that volume is now under direct threat from new target competition.
